documents.title: Guidance on the Use of AI in Teaching and Learning
documents.stance_why: It sets no single rule: "NIU affirms that faculty have primary responsibility for determining whether and how AI tools may be used in their courses" and offers three sample frameworks that faculty "may adapt".
documents.summary: University guidance leaving AI rules to faculty, with three adaptable syllabus options, disclosure expectations, assessment suggestions, privacy cautions and support resources.

units.why: The purpose statement says the guidance exists to "Support responsible, transparent and ethical uses of AI in teaching and learning", an institution-level statement of purpose, so P56 (framework/preamble) and phase general.
units.anchor: Support responsible, transparent and ethical uses of AI in teaching and learning.

units.why: Second stated aim: "Provide flexibility for faculty to determine appropriate use within their courses", which places the decision with each faculty member, so P04 (instructor sets the rule).
units.anchor: Provide flexibility for faculty to determine appropriate use within their courses.

units.why: The aim to "Align AI use with existing NIU policies on academic integrity, data privacy and intellectual property" ties AI use to existing policies; P77 (comply with existing policy) fits better than P56 because it names specific existing policy areas.
units.anchor: Align AI use with existing NIU policies on academic integrity, data privacy and intellectual property

units.why: The guidance states it "does not replace existing university policies" and offers only "shared language that faculty may adapt", which sets its scope and status, so P56 (scope statement).
units.anchor: This guidance does not replace existing university policies

units.why: Principle: "Decisions about AI use should be driven by learning outcomes, not the availability of tools." It is a stated principle for institutional AI decisions, so P56 rather than P41, which concerns limiting AI to protect practice.
units.anchor: Decisions about AI use should be driven by learning outcomes, not the availability of tools.

units.why: Principle: "Expectations for AI use should be clearly communicated to students in syllabi, assignments and course materials." This asks instructors to state AI expectations in syllabi, so P09, addressed to instructors.
units.anchor: clearly communicated to students in syllabi, assignments and course materials.

units.why: Principle: "Faculty should consider student access, cost, accessibility and potential bias when integrating AI tools." It is about equity and access (P51) and also bias.
units.anchor: Faculty should consider student access, cost, accessibility and potential bias
units.fit_note: Also asks faculty to consider potential bias in AI tools, which P51 does not cover; it frames consideration, not a ban on paid tools.

units.why: Principle: "AI use must align with NIU's academic integrity expectations, including proper attribution and disclosure when required." Primarily binds AI use to existing integrity rules (P77); disclosure is secondary and covered by separate units.
units.anchor: AI use must align with NIU's academic integrity expectations

units.why: Principle: "AI tools should support—rather than replace—critical thinking, creativity and disciplinary learning." Students' thinking must not be replaced by AI, matching P32.
units.anchor: AI tools should support—rather than replace—critical thinking, creativity and disciplinary learning.

units.why: The definition "artificial intelligence (AI) refers to computer systems ... that can perform tasks typically associated with human intelligence" sets what the guidance covers, so P61.
units.anchor: refers to computer systems (including software programs, websites and apps) that can perform tasks

units.why: The definition "Generative AI tools can create new text, images, audio, video or code in response to user prompts" defines the scope term used in the policy, so P61.
units.anchor: tools can create new text, images, audio, video or code in response to user prompts

units.why: Conduct and appropriate use of tools "including emerging technologies such as AI" are "guided by NIU's existing academic policies", so AI misuse is handled under existing academic integrity policies; P77 (existing policy) fits.
units.anchor: are guided by NIU's existing academic policies

units.why: "NIU is actively reviewing and updating guidance to make expectations related to AI use" says the guidance is provisional, so P54.
units.anchor: NIU is actively reviewing and updating guidance to make expectations related to AI use

units.why: "faculty have primary responsibility for determining whether and how AI tools may be used" puts the decision with instructors, so P04.
units.anchor: faculty have primary responsibility for determining whether and how AI tools may be used

units.why: "Acceptable use may vary by Discipline, Course level ... Learning objectives, Type of assignment" says rules differ across contexts, i.e. P04 (rule set per course/assignment).
units.anchor: Acceptable use may vary by

units.why: "Faculty are encouraged to make expectations explicit rather than assuming a single, institution-wide rule" asks faculty to state expectations (P09 communication); it also affirms no single rule, but the action requested is making rules explicit.
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged to make expectations explicit rather than assuming a single, institution-wide rule.

units.why: "Faculty should include one of the following policy approaches in their syllabus or assignment instructions" requires an AI statement in the syllabus or assignment, so P09.
units.anchor: Faculty should include one of the following policy approaches in their syllabus or assignment instructions.

units.why: The section "Sample Course Policy Frameworks (Faculty May Adapt)" offers three named options (not permitted, limited or guided, encouraged with transparency), i.e. named levels of AI use, so P05.
units.anchor: Sample Course Policy Frameworks (Faculty May Adapt)

units.why: Option 1 says "Students may not use generative AI tools to complete course assignments unless explicitly authorized", a default ban with authorization exceptions, so P01 (default prohibition); P06 does not fit as it is not about a silent syllabus.
units.anchor: Students may not use generative AI tools to complete course assignments unless explicitly authorized.

units.why: Option 1 adds "Use of AI-generated content without permission may be considered a violation of academic integrity", classifying unauthorized use as misconduct, so P36.
units.anchor: Use of AI-generated content without permission may be considered a violation of academic integrity.

units.why: Option 2 says students "may use AI tools for specific purposes (e.g., brainstorming, outlining, editing for clarity) as outlined in the assignment instructions"; narrow listed uses, nearest to P15 (brainstorming) though it also lists outlining and editing.
units.anchor: Students may use AI tools for specific purposes (e.g., brainstorming, outlining, editing for clarity)
units.frag_start: Students may use AI tools for
units.fit_note: Narrow list of permitted purposes also includes outlining and editing for clarity (writing support), not only brainstorming.

units.why: "Use beyond these purposes is not permitted" bans AI use outside the listed purposes; this is not a ban on producing submitted work (P19) or a default ban (P01) and is specific to the limited tier.
units.anchor: Use beyond these purposes is not permitted
units.policy: Use beyond the purposes listed in the assignment instructions is not permitted.
units.uncovered_note: Under the limited-use tier, any AI use outside the purposes listed in the assignment is not permitted.

units.why: Option 2 continues "and must be disclosed when required", a conditional disclosure duty, so P24.
units.anchor: must be disclosed when required
units.policy: AI use under the limited option must be disclosed when required.

units.why: Option 3 says "Students are encouraged to use AI tools as part of the learning process", welcoming AI use, so P02.
units.anchor: Students are encouraged to use AI tools as part of the learning process.

units.why: "students must document how they were used and reflect on their impact on learning" requires documentation and reflection on AI use, matching P26.
units.anchor: students must document how they were used and reflect on their impact on learning.

units.why: "Faculty are encouraged to specify: What tools are allowed or discouraged; What disclosure is required; How student work will be evaluated" asks instructors to state tool rules, disclosure and evaluation, so P09.
units.anchor: What tools are allowed or discouraged What disclosure is required

units.why: "When AI use is permitted, faculty may require students to: Acknowledge the use of AI tools" lets faculty require acknowledgement, matching P24.
units.anchor: faculty may require students to: Acknowledge the use of AI tools

units.why: "Describe how the tool was used (e.g., brainstorming, drafting, revising)" is a disclosure content item; nearest is P24 as it does not name tool, prompt or output (P25).
units.anchor: Describe how the tool was used (e.g., brainstorming, drafting, revising)
units.fit_note: Asks for a description of how the tool was used, not citation of tool, prompt or output.

units.why: "Retain responsibility for the accuracy, originality and integrity of submitted work" makes students responsible for what they submit, so P29.
units.anchor: Retain responsibility for the accuracy, originality and integrity of submitted work
units.fit_note: Framed as something faculty may require.

units.why: "Students remain accountable for meeting course learning outcomes, regardless of AI assistance" keeps students accountable whatever AI does, so P29.
units.anchor: Students remain accountable for meeting course learning outcomes, regardless of AI assistance.

units.why: Under Assessment and AI, "Emphasizing process, reflection and iteration" suggests redesigning assessment around AI, so P35.
units.anchor: Emphasizing process, reflection and iteration

units.why: "Incorporating in-class, oral or applied assessments" suggests assessment formats that check understanding without AI. P34 (oral) chosen; in-class weight shifts (P33) also appear.
units.anchor: Incorporating in-class, oral or applied assessments
units.fit_note: Also lists in-class and applied assessments, which is closer to P33.

units.why: "Designing assignments that require discipline-specific judgment or personal context" suggests assignment redesign around AI, so P35.
units.anchor: Designing assignments that require discipline-specific judgment or personal context

units.why: "Creating learning activities where students critically examine and evaluate AI outputs, limitations and impacts, rather than simply prohibiting AI use" redesigns activities around AI and prefers engaging with AI over bans; P35 chosen.
units.anchor: critically examine and evaluate AI outputs, limitations and impacts, rather than simply prohibiting AI use
units.fit_note: Also prefers critical engagement over prohibition, touching P31 and P44.

units.why: "many AI tools: Collect and store user data; May use submitted content for training purposes" warns of data practices, so P50.
units.anchor: Collect and store user data May use submitted content for training purposes

units.why: "Do not upload student work, grades or non-public instructional materials into public AI tools unless the tool has been institutionally approved" is a ban on uploading materials into AI, addressed to faculty and students, so P49.
units.anchor: Do not upload student work, grades or non-public instructional materials into public
units.fit_note: Also covers student work and grades (instructor data), and exempts institutionally approved tools.

units.why: "their use must align with NIU's Research Misconduct Policy" governs AI in research, so P62.
units.anchor: their use must align with NIU's Research Misconduct Policy

units.why: "AI tools should not be used in ways that undermine research integrity or ethical standards" is a rule on AI in research, so P62.
units.anchor: AI tools should not be used in ways that undermine research integrity or ethical standards.

units.why: "Faculty development workshops and consultations" listed under NIU support help faculty learn AI, so P63.
units.anchor: Faculty development workshops and consultations

units.why: "Academic integrity tutorials for students and faculty" offers training for students as well as faculty, so P70 rather than P63.
units.anchor: Academic integrity tutorials for students and faculty

units.why: "Student-facing AI literacy resources" are offered to students, so P70.
units.anchor: Student-facing AI literacy resources

units.why: "Library-supported guidance on research, citation and academic integrity" points students to library staff as human help, so P72.
units.anchor: Library-supported guidance on research, citation and academic integrity
units.fit_note: Not specific to AI; lists library guidance on research, citation and integrity.

units.why: "Additional training and resources will continue to be developed as AI technologies evolve" promises continued training; nearest is P70.
units.anchor: Additional training and resources will continue to be developed as AI technologies evolve.
units.fit_note: Commitment to develop more training over time, also governance-like.

documents.title: AI guidance for students
documents.stance_why: The page tells students "Your professor determines if and how AI technologies may be used in coursework" and sets no university-wide rule.
documents.summary: Student-facing page listing guidelines, NIU-licensed tools and training, and FAQs telling students to follow the syllabus, ask, disclose, and avoid plagiarism and misattribution.

units.why: "NIU is preparing students to navigate a world increasingly shaped by artificial intelligence" frames AI skills as preparation for the future, so P44.
units.anchor: NIU is preparing students to navigate a world increasingly shaped by artificial intelligence.

units.why: "By promoting responsible and innovative uses of AI in learning, NIU helps students build the knowledge and skills needed" states NIU promotes responsible, innovative AI use; P44 (skills for work).
units.anchor: promoting responsible and innovative uses of AI in learning
units.fit_note: Stated as promoting responsible and innovative use generally.

units.why: "The university continues to evaluate the impact of artificial intelligence on teaching" says the university is still assessing effects, so P54 (ongoing review).
units.anchor: The university continues to evaluate the impact of artificial intelligence on teaching
units.fit_note: Ongoing evaluation of impact, linked to P55.

units.why: "Faculty and staff are encouraged to stay informed about their responsibilities related to protecting the security and privacy of personal data and intellectual property" asks employees to protect data, so P50.
units.anchor: stay informed about their responsibilities related to protecting the security and privacy of personal data

units.why: "NIU provides a number of approved AI tools and technologies to support teaching and learning" offers sanctioned tools, so P17.
units.anchor: NIU provides a number of approved AI tools and technologies to support teaching and learning.

units.why: "NIU recommends that students, faculty and staff use only AI tools" recommends vetted tools for data protection, so P50.
units.anchor: NIU recommends that students, faculty and staff use only AI tools

units.why: "These tools have been licensed by NIU and are available to all NIU faculty" lists licensed AI tools (Adobe, Copilot, Quinncia), so P17.
units.anchor: These tools have been licensed by NIU and are available to all NIU faculty

units.why: "NIU's M365 license includes commercial data protection to safeguard sensitive university data" describes privacy protection of a licensed tool, so P50.
units.anchor: license includes commercial data protection to safeguard sensitive university data

units.why: "See the resources below to take advantage of the AI training and support currently available at NIU" points to AI tutorials, so P70.
units.anchor: take advantage of the AI training and support currently available at NIU.

units.why: "Your professor determines if and how AI technologies may be used in coursework" tells students the instructor decides, so P04.
units.anchor: Your professor determines if and how AI technologies may be used in coursework.

units.why: "check your syllabus and/or ask before using AI" tells students unsure about use to check and ask first, so P10.
units.anchor: If you’re not sure, check your syllabus and/or ask before using AI.

units.why: "Start with the syllabus and assignment instructions" tells students where to find the rules. No type covers telling students where to look; P10 is about asking, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Start with the syllabus and assignment instructions.
units.policy: Students start with the syllabus and assignment instructions to learn what AI use is allowed.
units.uncovered_note: Students are told to start with the syllabus and assignment instructions to learn what is allowed.

units.why: "If the course policy is unclear, contact your professor for guidance before using AI" is an ask-first rule, so P10.
units.anchor: If the course policy is unclear, contact your professor for guidance before using AI.

units.why: "Many faculty will require acknowledgement and/or citation when AI meaningfully contributes" says disclosure is often required, so P24.
units.anchor: Many faculty will require acknowledgement and/or citation when AI meaningfully contributes

units.why: "ranging from prohibited, to permitted with permission, to permitted with acknowledgement" describes a range of course policy examples, so P05.
units.anchor: ranging from prohibited, to permitted with permission, to permitted with acknowledgement

units.why: "Disclosure is always preferable to silence" advises students to disclose AI use, so P24 (P28 rejected because it does not state consequences).
units.anchor: Disclosure is always preferable to silence.

units.why: "If you used AI in any meaningful way, be transparent about how you used it" is a disclosure instruction, so P24.
units.anchor: be transparent about how you used it

units.why: "Clear, proactive disclosure helps protect you from misunderstandings and potential academic integrity concerns" says disclosure lowers risk, so P28.
units.anchor: Clear, proactive disclosure helps protect you from misunderstandings and potential academic integrity concerns.
units.fit_note: States disclosure protects the student but not that it is unpenalized.

units.why: "Don't submit AI-generated work as if it's solely your own if your professor doesn't allow it—or if disclosure is required" forbids submitting AI work as one's own where disallowed, so P19.
units.anchor: submit AI-generated work as if it’s solely your own if your professor doesn’t allow it
units.fit_note: Also covers undisclosed work where disclosure is required.

units.why: "academic dishonesty applies broadly in the academic environment" classes AI misuse under dishonesty rules, so P36.
units.anchor: academic dishonesty applies broadly in the academic environment

units.why: "research misconduct includes serious violations like claiming another person's or entity's work as your own" states misconduct definition, so P36.
units.anchor: research misconduct includes serious violations like claiming another person’s or entity’s work as your own

units.why: "AI tools can sometimes reproduce or closely paraphrase copyrighted material without citation" explains a copyright and plagiarism risk, so P52.
units.anchor: AI tools can sometimes reproduce or closely paraphrase copyrighted material without citation
units.fit_note: Concerns plagiarism risk of reproduced text more than licensing.

units.why: "Submitting AI-generated text that closely mirrors existing books, articles or websites" is listed as a plagiarism risk, so P36.
units.anchor: Submitting AI-generated text that closely mirrors existing books, articles or websites

units.why: "Copying or lightly editing AI output that reproduces ideas or language from a real author" is a listed plagiarism pitfall, so P36.
units.anchor: Copying or lightly editing AI output that reproduces ideas or language from a real author

units.why: "Relying on AI-generated citations without checking the original sources" tells students to verify AI output, so P31.
units.anchor: Relying on AI-generated citations without checking the original sources

units.why: "Citing sources you have not personally read or verified" is a verification rule, so P31.
units.anchor: Citing sources you have not personally read or verified

units.why: "Read the original sources yourself" asks students to verify sources rather than trust AI, so P31.
units.anchor: Read the original sources yourself

units.why: "Write in your own words and academic voice" asks students to submit their own writing, so P29.
units.anchor: Write in your own words and academic voice

units.why: "Cite real authors and publications accurately" is a citation accuracy rule; nearest is P24.
units.anchor: Cite real authors and publications accurately
units.fit_note: Concerns accurate citation of real sources, not disclosure of AI use.

units.why: "Disclose permitted AI use when required by your professor" is a disclosure duty, so P24.
units.anchor: Disclose permitted AI use when required by your professor

units.why: "Become familiar with NIU’s Student Code of Conduct and course-specific AI policies" points students to existing conduct rules and course policies, so P77.
units.anchor: Become familiar with NIU’s Student Code of Conduct and course-specific AI policies

units.why: "ask your professor if you are unsure whether a particular use of AI is allowed" is an ask-first rule, so P10.
units.anchor: ask your professor if you are unsure whether a particular use of AI is allowed

units.why: "How you decide to engage with AI should be guided by these values" ties AI use to community values (Northern Pact), so P56.
units.anchor: How you decide to engage with AI should be guided by these values.
units.fit_note: Points to community values, not an AI-specific framework.

units.why: "If you rely on AI, you miss out on the benefits of learning which involves your own thinking" says AI use costs learning, so P41.
units.anchor: you miss out on the benefits of learning which involves your own thinking.

units.why: "Using AI eliminates the necessary friction to learn" is a productive-struggle rationale, so P41.
units.anchor: Using AI eliminates the necessary friction to learn.

units.why: "using AI simply to obtain answers also carries a real environmental cost" names environmental costs, so P53.
units.anchor: using AI simply to obtain answers also carries a real environmental cost

units.why: "worth weighing whether the educational benefit justifies the environmental impact" asks students to weigh environmental cost, so P53.
units.anchor: worth weighing whether the educational benefit justifies the environmental impact

units.why: The Student Guide offers "a comprehensive introduction to the opportunities and challenges that AI brings", an AI-literacy resource, so P70.
units.anchor: comprehensive introduction to the opportunities and challenges that AI brings

units.why: "Concise set of values and practices to guide responsible, equitable, and transparent use of AI" describes the AI Ethical Guidelines, an institution-level framework, so P56.
units.anchor: Concise set of values and practices to guide responsible, equitable, and transparent use of AI

units.why: "Information and tutorials provided by NIU Libraries about using AI-assisted tools in your literature search" offers library AI training, so P70.
units.anchor: Information and tutorials provided by NIU Libraries about using AI-assisted tools

notes: Coder B. Course layer deferred; no school or computing unit policy found.
